what_this_is: The outcome gate of ADR-0085, widened to the paths that actually get heavy by ADR-0087: what importing each of the runtime's real import chains in a pristine child process loads, and what it costs in resident memory. Read by tests/test_runtime_footprint.py. Regenerate, do not hand-edit.

budget_rule.basis: Calibrated on the entry_point path, the lightest one and the only one numpy is absent from: putting numpy on it takes the working set to 66.96 MiB, 2.96 MiB over that path's budget of 64.00 MiB. numpy is the lightest heavy native dependency this project installs at all, so it is the hardest realistic case. One calibration speaks for every path because every budget is `worst observed run + 4.0 MiB` rounded up: what a budget catches is that headroom, which is the same everywhere, not the level the budget sits at. If this margin ever reads UNDER, the headroom has stopped guarding anything and must be tightened; tests/test_runtime_footprint.py fails on a record that says so.

module_count.basis: len(sys.modules) after importing vspeech.main. N=10 consecutive runs: min 716, max 716 (spread 0). Budget = max + 16. ADR-0085 requires this indicator to catch pydantic_settings, measured at +31 modules on the entry point (N=10), so the slack is held below that signal -- slightly over half of it, not under -- while still absorbing the submodule shuffle of a routine dependency upgrade.

resident_memory_mib.basis: Working set (GetProcessMemoryInfo) of the child itself after importing vspeech.main. N=10 consecutive runs: min 58.43, median 58.73, max 59.02 MiB -- spread 0.59 MiB (1.0% of the median). Budget = max + 4.0 MiB headroom rounded up, i.e. 4.98 MiB of headroom, about 8x the observed spread, so it does not flap. What this indicator deliberately does not catch is pydantic_settings' ~1.5 MiB of cost unique to the entry point (N=10; ADR-0085) -- the module indicators cover that, which is why there are two.
